box.description: Extracts all the text inside a bordered box in your document. Specify a word or phrase that's printed in or near the box, and Sensible finds the box automatically.
box.position: Adjusts where Sensible starts searching for the box border, relative to the anchor text. Use this if the default starting point lands on the border itself and Sensible can't recognize the box.
box.offsetX: Shifts the box-search starting point left or right by inches. Use when the anchor is outside the box and you need to move it inside the border.
box.offsetY: Shifts the box-search starting point up or down by inches. Use when the anchor is outside the box and you need to move it inside the border.
box.percentOverlapX: Controls how much of a line's width must fall inside the box for Sensible to extract it. Lower the default (0.9) if lines overlapping box borders aren't getting extracted.
box.percentOverlapY: Controls how much of a line's height must fall inside the box for Sensible to extract it. Lower the default (0.8) if lines overlapping box borders aren't getting extracted.
box.offsetBoxes: Navigates from the anchor's box to a neighboring box by counting shared borders in a given direction. Use for tables or grids where each cell shares its borders with its neighbors, as a workaround when not all boxes have anchoring text.
box.darknessThreshold: Sets how dark a pixel must be for Sensible to treat it as a box border. Lower the default (0.9) for boxes with dark or scanned backgrounds.
box.includeAnchor: When true, includes the anchor text itself in the output if it falls inside the box borders. By default the anchor is excluded.
box.sortLines: When misaligned text (like handwriting) gets extracted in the incorrect order, correct it by forcing Sensible to read it left to right. Recommended.
box.tiebreaker: When a box contains multiple lines, specifies which one to return. For example, `first` for the top left line, `last` for the bottom right, or join to combine them all into a single string.
box.xRangeFilter: Limits extraction to a column-like slice of the box defined by a starting vertical edge and width in inches. For example, use when the box contains multiple columns and you only want one. As an alternative, use the Multicolumn preprocessor.

intersection.description: Extracts the value at the point where a row and a column cross, like looking up a cell in a spreadsheet by naming both its row and column. More reliable than the Row method for tables with empty cells, and works in any grid-like layout.
intersection.verticalAnchor: Identifies the column by specifying its heading. Sensible draws a vertical line through this text and extracts whatever sits where it meets the field anchor's row.
intersection.horizontalAnchor: Identifies the row by specifying its label. Use instead of verticalAnchor when the field anchor is a column heading, typically combined with `"match": "all"` to extract multiple cells across a row in one field.
intersection.offsetX: Use when the target data is slightly offset from the column heading's center. Shifts the vertical axis line left or right by inches.
intersection.offsetY: Use when the target data is slightly offset from the row label's center. Shifts the horizontal axis up or down by inches.
intersection.width: Sets the width of the capture region at the intersection point, in inches. Without this, Sensible extracts any text touching the exact intersection point; a non-zero value captures a wider horizontal slice.
intersection.height: Sets the height of the capture region at the intersection point, in inches. Without this, Sensible extracts any text touching the exact intersection point; a non-zero value captures a taller vertical slice.
intersection.percentOverlapX: Controls how much of a line's width must fall inside the capture region for Sensible to extract it. Lower the default (0.9) if lines overlapping the region's borders aren't getting extracted.
intersection.percentOverlapY: Controls how much of a line's height must fall inside the capture region for Sensible to extract it. Lower the default (0.8) if lines overlapping the region's borders aren't getting extracted.
intersection.sortLines: When misaligned text gets extracted in the incorrect order, correct it by forcing Sensible to read it left to right. Recommended.
intersection.tiebreaker: When the intersection region contains multiple lines, specifies which one to return. For example, first for the top left line, last for the bottom right, or join to combine them all into a single string.
intersection.xRangeFilter: Limits extraction to a column-like slice of the intersection region defined by a starting vertical edge and width in inches. Use when the region contains multiple columns and you only want one.

checkbox: Extracts whether a checkbox is checked or unchecked. Specify a word printed to the left or right of it, and Sensible searches in that direction to find the checkbox.
nearestCheckbox: Extracts whether a checkbox is checked or unchecked. Specify a word or phrase printed anywhere near the checkbox, and Sensible finds the closest one automatically.
